findings.issue: typescript ^7.0.2 is the native Go compiler, stable only since July 2026; TS6/TS7 behavioral gaps could still surface in edge cases and pinning is loose (^7.0.2).
findings.suggestion: Fine to keep — it is the official stable release — but verify the tsc build in CI on the same version and consider an exact pin if reproducibility matters, since the toolchain is months old.

findings.issue: @hono/node-server v2.x is a 2026 major (perf rewrite) with identical public API; upgrades within v2 have already carried security fixes (e.g. the serveStatic path-decoding fix in v2.1.3, Sept 2026).
findings.suggestion: Keep the ^2 range and stay current on patch releases, which is what the app already does (^2.1.5).

summary: The app is built entirely on stable, current-generation APIs: Hono v4 (the stable line while v5 is still RC), @hono/node-server v2, htmx 2 and plain Node/htmx primitives, with no experimental, preview or unstable markers anywhere. The only recent items are the TypeScript 7 toolchain and the node-server v2 adapter, both official stable releases isolated to the build script and one file respectively. There is essentially no experimental risk to manage.
